questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: The maintenance of favourable internal conditions, by self-regulated mechanisms, even though there are changes in the environment, is known as
questions.solution: For metabolic processes to continue, the living things need to remain in a steady state maintained by a self-regulatory mechanism called homeostasis.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Density of population increases when _________.
questions.solution: Natality is defined as the birth rate of a population. In general, natality covers the production of new individuals which arises from hatching, germination or arises by fission. Population density is directly proportional to birth rate.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which type of population interaction is found between clown fish and sea anemone?
questions.solution: Commensalism is a relation between individuals of two species in which one species is benefitted while the other organism is neither harmed nor benefitted. A commensal relation based on shelter is seen in clown fishes, which live unharmed among the stinging tentacles of sea anemones, where they are protected from predators. The anemone does not appear to derive any benefit by hosting the clown fish.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: The reason for the population explosion in the world is
questions.solution: The factors which favours population growth is increased natality (birth rate), decreased mortality (death rate), immigration, increase in life span and better medical facilities.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: The plants that grow on saline soils with a high concentration of NaCl<sub>2</sub>, MgSO<sub>4,</sub> and MgCl<sub>2</sub> are called
questions.solution: Halophytes are the plants growing in and tolerating very salty soil typical offshores of tidal river estuaries, salt marshes, or alkali desert flats. Generally, these soils (saline) have a very high concentration of salts like NaCl<sub>2</sub>, MgSO<sub>4</sub>, and MgCl<sub>2</sub>.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: In increasing order of organizational complexity, which one of the following is the correct sequence?
questions.solution: Species are a grouping of individuals resembling each other in important morphological, anatomical, and biochemical characters and can potentially interbreed. The population is an aggregation or grouping of individuals of the same species at the same time in a particular area.  The biotic community is an assemblage of interdependent, and the ecosystem is a self-sufficient and self-regulating segment of nature comprising of a biotic community and its physical environment, both interacting and exchanging materials.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Adaptation in organisms can be
questions.solution: Adaptation is an attribute of the organism (morphological, physiological, behavioural) that enables the organism to survive and reproduce in its habitat. Many adaptations have evolved over a long evolutionary time and are genetically fixed. However, these may remain epigenetic (not fixed genetically).

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: If birth and death rates were equal, a zero population growth rate would result. It is known as
questions.solution: In the long term, zero population growth can be achieved when the birth rate of a population equals the death rate, i.e. fertility is at replacement level and birth and death rates are stable, a condition also called demographic equilibrium.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: When environmental conditions are favourable, then the population growth curve will be
questions.solution: The J-shaped growth curve is shown by a small population reared in a natural environment with plenty of food but no predator. In this case, there is a rapid increase in population until the food is available, but after the decrease in the availability of food, there is a sudden increase in mortality rate and it is called population crash. E.g. Many insect populations show exponential growth and increase in their population size in the rainy season but are followed by a population crash at the end of the rainy season.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Certain species of wasps are seen to frequently visit flowering fig trees. The interaction between them is:
questions.solution:
Mutualism is the way two organisms of different species exist in a relationship in which each individual benefits. Similar interactions within a species are known as co-operation. The associations between tree roots and certain fungi Mycorrhiza is usually of mutual benefit (symbiotic): a delicate balance between the host plant and symbiont relations results in enhanced nutritional support for each member.

In this case, the female wasps use the fruit not only as oviposition (egg-laying) site but use the developing seeds within the fruit for nourishing its larvae. In turn, wasps help the plants in their pollination. In the favour of pollination, the fig offers the wasp some of its developing seeds.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: The capacity of an environment to pull on a limited number of individuals is known as
questions.solution: Carrying capacity refers to the size of a population that can be maintained indefinitely. Carrying capacity is the maximum number of individuals of a given species that an area's resources can sustain indefinitely without significantly depleting or degrading those resources.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which of the following is not a character of r-selected species?
options: A high energy allocation to reproduction
questions.solution: r-selected species are those that emphasize high growth rates, typically exploit less-crowded ecological niches, and produce many offspring, each of which has a relatively low probability of surviving to adulthood (i.e., high r, low K). Because of high growth rate their generation time is less.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Desert plants are generally
questions.solution: Succulent plants are fleshy xerophytes, which can grow in low water level areas (desert). That is why they are called desert plants.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
The age pyramid for human population is shown below.

Which of the following conclusion can be drawn from the given age pyramid?
options: It represents that the population is young and growing.
It is a pyramid of declining population.
It shows that the population is stable.
It shows that the population size is fluctuating.
questions.solution:
An age pyramid is a structural representation of age distribution (percent individuals of a given age or age group) plotted for the population. 

The given population age pyramid is a graphic representation of a young or growing population that appears like a triangle. The population has a very high proportion of pre-reproductive individuals, proportionate numbers of reproductive individuals are moderate, and post-reproductive individuals are proportionately fewer. The population is said to be expanding or increasing type.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: A high density of tiger population in an area can result in
questions.solution: A high density of tiger population in an area can result in intraspecific competition.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: What are the adaptations seen in animals that live in water scarcity conditions?
options: Having a thick coat to minimise evaporative desiccation
Oxidising stored fat to produce water as by product
Producing very concentrated urine and solid faeces
questions.solution: Kangaroo and desert rat seldom drink water. It has a thick coat to minimise evaporative desiccation. The animal seldom comes out of its comparatively humid and cool burrow during the day time <math><mn>90</mn><mi>%</mi></math> of its water requirement is met from metabolic water which is produced by respiratory breakdown of fats. <math><mn>10</mn><mi>%</mi></math> is obtained from food. Loss of water is minimised by producing nearly solid urine and faces.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: The term 'niche' of a species refers to
options: The specific place where an organism lives and the role it plays
questions.solution: A niche refers to the habitat of the organism and the functional role performed by the organism in its habitat. Niche is the unique character of an organism and two organisms cannot occupy the same niche at the same time and coexist in nature if they tend to do so than competition occurs and eventually one gets eliminated this is Gause competitive exclusion principle.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Organisms that can tolerate and thrive in a wide range of temperature are called
questions.solution: Eurythermal organisms can tolerate large changes in temperature. Stenothermal are those organisms that only survive in a narrow temperature range. Homeotherms have constant and relatively high body temperature. Poikilotherms are organisms that cannot regulate their body temperature.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: The egrets always forage close to where the cattle are grazing. The interaction between them can be called
questions.solution: This is the interaction in which one species benefits and the other is neither harmed nor benefited. The egrets always forage close to where the cattle are grazing because the cattle, as they move, stir up and flush out insects from the vegetation that otherwise might be difficult for the egrets to find and catch. The egrets get benefitted while the cattle are neither benefitted nor harmed.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which one of the following is a matching pair of certain organism(s) and the kind of association?
options: Red algae and fungi in liches  - Mutualism
Cuscuta (dodder) growing on other flowering plants  -  Epiphysis
questions.solution: A classic example of commensalism is observed in the interaction between a sea anemone that has stinging tentacles and the clownfish that lives among them. The fish gets protection from predators which stay away from the stinging tentacles. The anemone does not appear to derive any benefit by hosting the clownfish.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Select the incorrectly matched pair.
options: Goats and Abingdon tortoise on Galapagos Islands–Competition
questions.solution:
The relationship exhibited by Cuscuta and hedge plant is parasitism. In this interaction, Cuscuta obtains nutrients directly from the hedge plant by producing haustoria and inserting them into the vascular system of the host. Cuscuta is a holoparasite, thus it is completely dependent on the host for all the requirements.

Commensalism: Interaction in which one species benefits and other is neither harmed nor benefited. The species which is benefitted is termed commensal and the other species is called the host. Such a population interaction is represented as (+,0).

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Plants growing in shady region are called
questions.solution: Those plants which grow best in shade or diffused light are called sciophytes or heliophobous or photophobous or shade-loving plants.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Study the following columns and choose the correct option.
 
  Column-I   Column- II
(A) Population (1) Part of the earth consisting of all the ecosystems of the world
(B) Community (2) assemblage of all the individuals belonging to different species occurring in an area
(C) Ecosystem (3) Group of similar individuals belonging to the same species found in an area
(D) Ecosphere (4) Interaction between the living organisms and their physical environment components
    (5) Classification of organisms based on the type of environment
questions.solution:
Ecology is basically concerned with four levels of biological organization – organisms, populations, communities, ecosystems, and biomes.

A population is a group of similar individuals in a particular geographical area or space. Community is the assemblage of interdependent and interacting populations of different species present in an area. The ecosystem is the sum of the biotic (living) and abiotic (non-living) components of a particular geographical area. The biosphere also called the ecosphere or giant ecosystem is the largest and nearly self-sufficient biological system. It is formed of all the ecosystems of the world. It is also called the "life-supporting zone" of the earth.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: The graph shows two types of the population growth curve, 'a' - Exponential and 'b' - Logistic. Which of the following graph models is considered to be the more realistic one?
questions.solution:
(i) A—Exponential growth curve and B—Logistic growth curve
(ii) Logistic growth curve B is considered more realistic one because the resources are finite and become limited sooner or later.
(iii) K stands for carrying capacity which refers to the maximum number of individuals of a population that the given environment can sustain at a given time.
(iv) N symbolises population density, i.e. the number of individuals of a species in a given population per unit area.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: If the birth rate is 100, the death rate is 10 and the number of individuals in a population group is 1000, then what will be the intrinsic rate of natural increase of the population?
questions.solution:
The increase in the number of individuals in a particular time period is termed as ‘birth rate’ or ‘natality’, while the individuals dying over a time period are known as ‘mortality’ or ‘death rate’.
Birth rate = 100
Death rate = 10
Number of individuals in a population = 1000
The intrinsic rate of natural increase is = 100 – 10 = 90

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Adaptations to plants against dry environmental conditions is/are
options: Stomata remain open during day time
More than one option is correct
questions.solution: Many desert plants have a thick cuticle on their leaf surfaces and have their stomata arranged in deep pits (sunken) to minimize water loss through transpiration. They also have a special photosynthetic pathway (CAM) that enables their stomata to remain closed during day time. Some desert plants like Opuntia, have no leaves and the photosynthetic function is taken over by the flattened stems.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Biotic potential refers to
options: Increase of population under optimum conditions
Increase of population under given conditions
Increase of population under natural conditions
Increase of population under climatic conditions
questions.solution: The biotic potential is described by the unrestricted growth of populations resulting in the maximum growth of that population. The biotic potential is the highest possible vital index of a species; therefore, when the species has its highest birthrate and lowest mortality rate.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: The study of trends in human population growth and the prediction of future development is known as
questions.solution: Demography is the study of human population growth and prediction of future development. Some of the attributes of the population are used to estimate its growth as population size and may fluctuate in a given habitat during a given period of time.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: The population of an insect species shows an explosive increase in numbers during rainy season followed by its disappearance at the end of the season. What does the pattern of population show?
options: S-shaped or sigmoid growth of this insect
The food plants mature and die at the end of rainy season
Its population growth curve is of J-type
The population of its predators increases enormously
questions.solution: Its population growth curve is J-shaped in which density increases rapidly in exponential fashion and then stops abruptly as environmental resistance or another limiting factor becomes effective more or less suddenly. Any species growing exponentially under unlimited resource conditions can reach enormous population densities in a short time.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: The main cause of the population explosion in the World is
questions.solution: The main cause of population explosion in the World is excellent health care as the better medical facilities controls the incidence and spread of the disease. Many of the fatal diseases, epidemics and proper care of new born children and their mothers decreases the death rate and hence enhances the population growth.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which of the following set of examples is correct with respect to escaping time as a response to abiotic factors?
options: Bacteria, fungi and all plants - Thick spores
questions.solution: Bears going into hibernation during winter is an example of escape in time. Some snails and fish go into aestivation to avoid summer–related problems-heat and desiccation. Under unfavourable conditions, many zooplankton species in lakes and ponds are known to enter diapause, a stage of suspended development.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Mark the correct pair.
questions.solution: A diapause is a form of developmental arrest in zooplanktons that is much like hibernation in higher animals.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Ecologically, the most important factor that controls the distribution of organism on Earth is
questions.solution: Ecologically temperature is most important factor because it controls distribution of organism on earth. On the basis of temperature tolerance, both plants and animals show a distribution pattern on earth. Temperature affects all physiological functions of organisms through its effect on enzyme activity.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Limit of the environment to support a population is called its
questions.solution: In ecological terms, the carrying capacity of an ecosystem is the size of the community or population that can be supported indefinitely upon the available resources and services of that ecosystem. Living within the limits of an ecosystem depends on three factors: the number of resources available in the ecosystem, the size of the population or community and the number of resources each individual within the community is consuming.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Population density of terrestrial organisms is measured in terms of individual per
questions.solution: Population density of terrestrial organisms is measured in terms of number of individuals per meter square while the population density of aquatic organisms is measured in terms of number of individuals per cubic meter.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: A high density of a protected animal in a national park can result in
questions.solution:
Competition between organisms of the same species is called intraspecific competition. If the number of organisms gets increased then the competition for food, shelter, and other resources will also get increased.
Mutualism is an obligatory and mutually beneficial relationship occurring between two interacting organisms. Predation is the act of capturing, killing, and eating. It is a negative interaction between two organisms. Migration is individuals from a population for settling into a new area.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Mycorrhizae help in the absorption of
questions.solution: The roots of higher plants possess symbiotic mycorrhizae. It is a symbiotic, non-pathogenic association between the roots and soil fungi. Several conifers lack root hair and here the mycorrhizae perform this function. The mycorrhizae are of two types: ectomycorrhizae and endo-mycorrhizae with an intermediate category as ectondomycorrhizae. The most common endomycorrhizae are Vesicular Arbuscular Mycorrhizae (VAM), generally present in herbaceous plants. Mycorrhizae perform the function of root hair, i.e. they absorb essential ions.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Homeothermy is found in
questions.solution: The body temperature is constant in homeothermic (warm-blooded) animals such as birds and mammals. Rat is a mammal and a regulator, and it doesn't change its body temperature according to environmental temperature. The fishes, amphibians and reptiles are poikilothermic (cold-blooded) animals and change the body temperature according to the external temperature.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Competition for food, light and space is most severe between two
options: Distantly related species growing in different habitat
Distantly related species growing in the same habitat
Closely related species growing in different habitat
Closely related species growing in the same area
questions.solution: Closely related species have the same desire of food, light and space and in the same area these all requirements are found in a limited amount or quota. Hence competition for food, light and space is most severe between two closely related species growing in the same area.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: In the equation, dN/dt = rN
options: 'r' is called the ‘intrinsic rate of natural increase’.
'r' is the parameter chosen for assessing impacts of any biotic factor on population growth.
'r' is the parameter chosen for assessing impacts of an abiotic factor on population growth.
questions.solution:
The equation, dN/dt = rN describes the exponential or geometric growth pattern of a population and results in a J-shaped curve when N is plotted with relation to time.

The 'r' in this equation is called the ‘intrinsic rate of natural increase’ and is a very important parameter chosen for assessing impacts of any biotic or abiotic factor on population growth.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: The Abingdon tortoise became extinct on Galapagos island within a decade of the introduction of goats. This is an example of
questions.solution: The Abingdon tortoise in Galapagos islands became extinct within a decade only after goats were introduced on the island. It is an example of competitive exclusion. It happened due to the lesser browsing efficiency of the tortoise.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which of the following is a characteristic of an early community?
questions.solution: An ecological niche is the role and position a species has in its environment and describes how it meets its needs for food and shelter, how it survives and how it reproduces. A species' niche includes all of its interactions with the biotic and abiotic factors of its environment. Early community has broader niche, i.e., niche is less specialized.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: In a population of an area, natality was equal to mortality for a given time period. However, the population density of the population increased. Which of the following may be the reason for the increase?
options: Number of immigrants = number of emigrants
Number of immigrants > Number of emigrants
Number of immigrants <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo><</mo></math> Number of emigrants
questions.solution:
Natality and immigration contribute to an increase in population density, whereas mortality and emigration tend to decrease the size.

The density of a population (N) at time t can be expressed after a period of time (t + 1) as: 

N(t+1) = Nt + [ (B + I) - (D + E) ]

where B denotes the number of births,  I denotes the number of immigrants, D is the number of deaths and E is the number of emigrants.

If B = D, and N(t+1) > Nt, then I > E.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Species that have maximum influence on the ecosystem are called
questions.solution: Keystone species are those which have an extremely high impact on a particular ecosystem relative to its population. Keystone species are also critical for the overall structure and function of an ecosystem, and they influence other types of plants and animals making up that ecosystem.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Animals that can tolerate a narrow range of salinity are
questions.solution: Stenohaline: Steno means narrow, and haline means salt. A fish cannot handle a wide fluctuation in salt content in water. Many fresh water fishes tend to be stenohaline and die in environments of high salinity, such as oceans. Fish living in coastal estuaries and tide pools are often euryhaline (tolerant to changes in salinity) as they have life cycle requiring tolerance for both freshwater and seawater environments, e.g., Salmon.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which of the following is not an adaptation associated with flight in birds?
questions.solution:
Adaptations for flying in birds:

a. Presence of wings and feathers.
b. Air sacs in lungs.
c. Hollow or pneumatic bones.
d. Only left ovary is functional.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Plants adapted to low light intensity have
options: Larger photosynthetic unit size than the sun plants
Higher rate of carbon dioxide fixation than the sun plants
questions.solution: Plants adapted to low light intensity have larger photosynthetic unit size than the sun plants.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which one of the following adaptation is associated with a ‘mangrove plant’?
options: Capable of absorbing water rapidly and retaining it
Capable of minimizing water loss and facilitating aeration to underground parts
Capable of reducing transpiration and able to store absorbed water
Presence of well organized leaves that are adapted to absorb nitrogenous matter
questions.solution: Mangrove plants are capable to minimize water loss and facilitate aeration to underground parts.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: In the equation for S-shaped population growth <math><mfrac><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">d</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi></mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">d</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">t</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">r</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi><mfenced close="]" open="[" separators="|"><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">K</mi><mo>-</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi></mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">K</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow></mfenced></math>, r represents
questions.solution: In the logistic growth, per capita growth rate (r) depends on population size (N) and how close it is to carrying capacity (K). 'r' is the per capita rate of increase for a particular species under ideal conditions, and it varies from species to species. For instance, bacteria can reproduce much faster than humans and would have a higher maximum per capita rate of increase. The maximum population growth rate for a species is called its biotic potential. 'r' represents the intrinsic growth rate of a population.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: The number of death and birth in the last stage of sigmoid growth curve of a population will be
questions.solution: The last stage of sigmoid growth curve is called the stationary phase or asymptote phase. It is observed on reaching the carrying capacity, where birth rate becomes equal to death rate.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Transition zone between two biomes is called
questions.solution: An ecotone is a transition area between two biological communities. It is where two communities meet and integrate. It may be narrow or wide, and it may be local (the zone between a field and forest) or regional (the transition between forest and grassland ecosystems).

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Choose the correct sequence of stages of the growth curve for bacteria.
questions.solution: The growth curve for bacteria is sigmoid. The first phase is the phase of slow growth, the lag phase. The second phase is the period of accelerated growth, the log phase. The third phase is the phase when growth rate becomes stable, stationary phase. Finally, the growth rate declines.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: The biome in which the mean annual temperature is approximately between <math><msup><mrow><mn>20°</mn></mrow></msup><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></math> and <math><msup><mrow><mn>25°</mn></mrow></msup><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></math> and the mean annual precipitation is approximately between 150 cm to 450 cm is
questions.solution:
Major biomes are formed due to annual variations and intensity of temperature and annual variations in precipitation. The approximate mean annual temperature (MT) in °C and mean annual precipitation (MP) in cm of various biomes are

Temperate forest: MT: 20–25 and MP: 75–225

Conifer forest biome: MT: 0–15 and MP: 50–250

Alpine tundra biome: MT: -10–0 and MP: 10–125

Tropical forest: MT: 20–25 and MP: 150–450.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Niche overlap indicates
options: Sharing of resources in the same species
Mutualism between two species
Active co-operation between two species
Competition between two species for similar resources
questions.solution: Niche overlap indicates competition between two species for similar resources. This indicates their similar habitat requirement and competition if tropic niche/spatial niche is the same and food/space is limiting, e.g., two different parasites on the same host.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Intrinsic rate of natural increase is
options: The sum of birth rates and death rates
The difference between birth rates and death rates
The sum birth rate and immigration
The difference between sum of birth rate and immigration and sum of death rate and emigration
questions.solution: The intrinsic rate of natural increase, denoted by 'r' is the difference in the birth rate and death rate. The r-value of the Norway rat is 0.015, and the flour beetle it is 0.12. The r-value helps us in understanding the effects of biotic and abiotic factors on population growth.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Epiphytes growing on trees is an example of
questions.solution: Commensalism is the interaction in which one species benefits and the other is neither harmed nor benefited. When a epiphyte grows on a tree it gets exposure to sunlight and support but the tree is nether benefitted nor harmed.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: The intrinsic rate of natural increase for Indian human population according to the 2011 census was
questions.solution: The intrinsic rate of natural increase (r) is the difference between birth rate and death rate. According to the 2011 census, India has a birth rate of 21.8 per 1000 and death rate 7.1 per 1000 individuals. Thus, r = 21.8 - 7.1 = 14.7 per 1000, which is 0.0147.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: The graph in case of a population showing maximum intrinsic growth will be
questions.solution: Ideally, when resources in the habitat are unlimited, each species has the ability to realize fully its innate potential to grow in number, as Darwin observed while developing his theory of natural selection. Then the population grows in an exponential or geometric fashion. The J-shaped curve shows three stages-lag phase, exponential phase and crash phase.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which of these statements is correct?
options: Herbivores are more adversely affected by competition than carnivores.
Carnivores are more adversely affected by competition than herbivores.
Both herbivores and carnivores are equally affected by competition.
Both herbivores and carnivores are not affected by competition.
questions.solution: Plant compete with the environment and with others for mineral resources. Any deficiency of any nutrient or mineral in the environment affects plants first. When plants decrease, the food available to herbivores decreases, and they get affected. However, the effect of deficiency will come later in carnivores when all plants and herbivores die.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: An association essential and beneficial to both the partners is observed between:
questions.solution: Mutualism is defined in a way that reflects the positive signs characterizing the outcome of their interactions, that is, as interactions between individuals of different species that benefit both of them. Orchids show a bewildering diversity of floral patterns many of which have evolved to attract the right pollinator insect (bees and bumblebees) and ensure guaranteed pollination by it (Figure 13.7). Not all orchids offer rewards. The Mediterranean orchid Ophrys employs ‘sexual deceit’ to get pollination done by a species of bee.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: The salt concentration is 30–35 (salinity in parts per thousand) in
questions.solution: The salt concentration (measured as salinity in parts per thousand) is less than 5 in inland waters, 30-35 in the sea and  <math><mo>></mo><mn>100</mn></math>  in some hypersaline lagoons.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Which of the following statements regarding species interdependence are true?

I. An association of two species where one is benefitted and other remains unaffected is called mutualism.
II. An interspecific association where both partners derive benefit from each other is called commensalism.
III. A direct food relation between two species of animals in which one animal kills and feeds on another is referred to as predation.
IV. A relationship between two species of organisms where both the partners are benefitted from each other is called symbiosis.
questions.solution:
Predation is a direct food relation between two species of animals, in which one animal (the predator) captures and feeds on another (the prey).
In symbiosis, two organisms live together in close physical association from which one or both derive benefit.
Mutualism: It confers benefits on both the interacting species. It is an obligate association of two organisms where two organisms often live together and cannot live separately.
Commensalism is the interaction in which one species benefits and other is neither harmed nor benefited. The species which is benefitted is termed commensal and the other species is called host.

questions.solution: In higher plants, seeds and some other vegetative reproductive structures serve as means to tide over periods of stress besides helping in dispersal – they germinate to form new plants under favourable moisture and temperature conditions. They do so by reducing their metabolic activity and going into a state of ‘dormancy’. In animals, the organism, if unable to migrate, might avoid the stress by escaping in time. The familiar case of bears going into hibernation during winter is an example of escape in time. Some snails and fish go into aestivation to avoid summer–related problems-heat and dessication. Under unfavourable conditions many zooplankton species in lakes and ponds are known to enter diapause, a stage of suspended development.

questions.solution: The process of formation of new species takes time. The environment should be relatively constant to have more species formation. questions.solution: The region near the middle of the Earth between the Tropic of Cancer and Tropic of Capricorn is considered as the tropic region. questions.solution: If a predator is too efficient and overexploits its prey, then the prey might become extinct and following it, the predator will also become extinct for lack of food. This is the reason why predators in nature are ‘prudent’. Prey species have evolved various defenses to lessen the impact of predation. Predators also help in maintaining species diversity in a community, by reducing the intensity of competition among competing prey species. Besides acting as ‘conduits’ for energy transfer across trophic levels, predators play other important roles. They keep prey populations under control.

If the environmental conditions are not met then the population will keep decreasing until the resources rebound.

questions.solution:
Adaptation is any attribute of the organism (morphological, physiological, behavioural) that enables the organism to survive and reproduce in its habitat. Many adaptations have evolved over a long evolutionary time and are genetically fixed.

Some organisms show behavioural responses to cope up with variations in their environment. Desert lizards lack the physiological ability that mammals have to deal with the high temperatures of their habitat, but manage to keep their body temperature fairly constant by behavioural means. They bask in the sun and absorb heat when their body temperature drops below the comfort zone, but move into shade when the ambient temperature starts increasing. Some species are capable of burrowing into the soil to hide and escape from the above-ground heat.

Graphical representation of the population growth is referred to as population growth curve. There are four phases of growth curve-

questions.solution: Brood parasitism in birds is a fascinating example of parasitism in which the parasitic bird lays its eggs in the nest of its host and lets the host incubate them. E.g. cuckoo laying its eggs in nest of crow.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: A group of individuals from different species living in the same habitat and exhibiting functional interactions is called:
questions.solution: A group of individual of same species living in a habitat forms a population and group of different population living in same habitat and exhibiting functional interaction forms a biotic community. Group of different population together forms a community.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: For a population at carrying capacity:
questions.solution: Carrying capacity is the maximum population that can be sustained is a particular area. In other words, the number organisms can survive normally in a particular area. The main limiting factor for the carrying capacity is the resources available in the area or the environmental factors. If the environmental conditions are not met then the population will keep decreasing until the resources rebound. At carrying capacity, the population stabilizes and have the rate of mortality same as the rate of natality.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Mammals from colder climates generally have shorter ears and limbs to minimise heat loss. This is
questions.solution: Ecogeographical rule formulated by Joel Asaph Allen broadly says that warm blooded animals of cold habitat have extremities like feet, tail, ears, etc. smaller compared to their relatives of warmer habitat. The enables to reduce heat loss by the organism.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Consider the following statements.

A. Temperature is the most ecologically relevant environmental factor.
B. Temperature increases progressively from the equator towards the poles and from plains to the mountain tops.
C. Diversity is not an important characteristic of living organisms.
D. Mango trees do not and cannot grow in temperate countries like Canada and Germany.

Of the above statements:
questions.solution: One of the most important factors of ecology is the temperature that varies seasonally. Also, physiological functions, morphology and the geographical distribution of organisms is affected by temperature. Temperature decreases progressively from the equator towards the poles and from plains to the mountain tops. Mango requires higher temperature for tis growth and development and lower temperatures through enzymes, if influences basal metabolism, activity and other physiological functions of the organism. Thus, Mango trees do not and cannot grow in temperate countries like Canada and Germany. All living organisms have several characteristics like growth, reproduction, sensitivity, nutrition, movement, respiration, excretion. Diversity is considered an important characteristic of living organisms as it provides information on its origin and inter-relationship with other organisms and environment.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: If a population of 50 Paramecium present in a pool increases to 150 after an hour, what would be the growth rate of the population?
questions.solution:
Population of paramecium at time t=50

Population of Paramecium at time(After one hour) =150

Growth rate of population =150-50=100 per hour

So the correct answer is D.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Pollination in Ophrys, a Mediterranean orchid (see figure below) occurs by
options: insects using the fruit as an oviposition site
insects feeding on its nectar for nutrition
bees due to the fragrance emitted by the orchid
questions.solution: Orchids show a bewildering diversity of floral patterns many of which have evolved to attract the right pollinator insect (bees and bumblebees) and ensure guaranteed pollination by it. Not all orchids offer rewards. The Mediterranean orchid Ophrys employs ‘sexual deceit’ to get pollination done by a species of bee. One petal of its flower bears an uncanny resemblance to the female of the bee in size, colour and markings. The male bee is attracted to what it perceives as a female, ‘pseudocopulates’ with the flower, and during that process is dusted with pollen from the flower. When this same bee ‘pseudocopulates’ with another flower, it transfers pollen to it and thus, pollinates the flower.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Competition is a rivalry between two or more organisms for obtaining the same resources. It is a type of
questions.solution: Competition is an interaction between organisms or species in which both the organisms or species are harmed. Limited supply of at least one resource (such as food, water, and territory) used by both can be a factor.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Which of the following statement/s is/are WRONG?

I. Mammals from colder climates generally have shorter ears and limbs to minimise heat loss.
II. The UV component of the spectrum is harmful to many organisms.
III. The tiger census in our national parks and tiger reserves is often based on actual headcounts.
IV. Some desert plants like Opuntia, have no leaves - they are reduced to spines.
V. In brood parasitism, the parasitic bird lays its eggs in the nest of its host and does not allow the host incubate them.
questions.solution:
Mammals from colder climates generally have shorter ears and limbs to minimise heat loss. This is called the Allen’s rule.

Exposure to higher concentration of UV rays can lead to mutation resulting in skin cancer. It can also cause permanent damage to the eyes by destroying the retinal cells. UV rays have been found to cause mutational changes in the immune cells and reducing the immune system.

In our country, every year, the tiger census is carried out based on their pug marks and fecal pellets of the tigers to determine the number of tigers in our country.

Some desert plants like Opuntia have adapted to survive in the extreme conditions by modifying their leaves to spine that reduces transpiration. Also, the stem is modified in thick flattened green structure that can perform photosynthesis.

Brood parasitism in birds is a fascinating example of parasitism in which the parasitic bird lays its eggs in the nest of its host and lets the host incubate them. During the course of evolution, the eggs of the parasitic bird have evolved to resemble the host’s egg in size and colour to reduce the chances of the host bird detecting the foreign eggs and ejecting them from the nest.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Deserts, grasslands, forests and tundra are the examples of:
questions.solution: Group of all ecosystem present in a large geographical area having similar climatic condition is called as biome. Deserts, grasslands, forests and tundra are all biomes and they occupy large geographical area having a specific set of characteristics.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: In general, species diversity ............... as we move away from the equator towards the poles and with very few exceptions, tropics harbor <math><mo>…......</mo><mo>…</mo></math> species than temperate or polar areas.
questions.solution:
Biodiversity includes all the flora and fauna on Earth. All the varieties of organisms come under biodiversity.

The region near the middle of the Earth between the Tropic of Cancer and Tropic of Capricorn is considered as the tropic region. This region receives the most amount of solar energy which leads to better productivity and higher species diversity. Also, the seasonal variations in such regions are low and environment mainly remains the same supporting high species richness and promoting niche specialization. Species-area relationship show a rectangular hyperbolic function. With very few exceptions, tropics harbour more species than temperate or polar areas. A forest in a tropical region like Equador has up to ten as many species of amphibians as a forest of equal area in a temperate region like the midwest of the USA.

Temperate regions include the subtropics and polar circles. These regions faced glaciation during the ice age which was not observed in the tropic regions.

When the diversity in organisms at the species level is termed as species diversity. Species diversity decreases as we move towards the poles can be for various reasons as - temperature decreases and conditions become harsh, the amount of solar radiation decreases including intensity, reduction in resources and vegetation for survival.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Why predator are prudent in nature?
options: They do not over exploit its prey
They are too efficient to kill their prey
questions.solution: Predators are prudent in nature, if predator is too efficient and overexploits its prey, then the prey might become extinct and following it, the predator will also become extinct for lack of food.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: The salinity of the sea measured in parts per thousand is:
questions.solution: The salt concentration (measured as salinity in parts per thousand), is less than 5 in inland waters, 30-35 in the sea and > 100 in some hypersaline lagoons. Some organisms are tolerant of a wide range of salinities (euryhaline) but others are restricted to a narrow range (stenohaline).

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: The Arctic tern is a bird which travels from the Arctic to the Antarctic region and then back again. Hence it sees two summers in a year. On an average, Arctic terns travel a distance of 70,000 km annually. This is an example of:
questions.solution:
There are four major ways through which an organism can cope with stressful conditions:

By regulating the constant body temperature, by changing their body temperature with ambient temperature found in animals that cannot maintain constant body temperature known as conforming, some animals migrate to the comfortable area and return when the stressful period gets over, by forming thick walled spores that help to survive in stressful condition (e.g. in bacteria, fungi and lower plants) and this response is called 'suspend'. The response observed here is migration. During winter many animals, especially birds, take on long distance migration to friendlier environment.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which of the following would necessarily decrease the density of a population in a given habitat?
questions.solution:
The mortality rate is the measure of number of deaths in a particular population for a particular time period. It is denoted by letter D.

The rate of emigration is the number of people leaving/exiting an area of population at a particular time interval.

Natality rate also called birth rate for a population. It is a measure of number of births occurring in a population in a particular time period. It is denoted by letter B

The rate of immigration, which is the number of people entering an area of population at a particular time interval.

If mortality and emigration are in higher number than natality and immigration, the population density with decrease.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Find out the incorrect statement.
options: Archaebacteria flourish in hot springs and deep sea hydrothermal vents where temperature far exceed <math><mn>100</mn><mo>°</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></math>.
Many fish thrive in Antarctic waters where the temperature is always below zero.
A large variety of marine invertebrates and fish live at great depths in the ocean where the pressure could be <math><mo>></mo><mn>100</mn></math> times the normal atmospheric pressure.
Desert lizard have physiological ability that mammals have to deal with the high temperature of their habitat.
questions.solution: Some organisms show behavioural responses to cope up with variations in their environment. Desert lizards lack the physiological ability that mammals have to deal with the high temperatures of their habitat, but manage to keep their body temperature fairly constant by behavioural means. They bask in the sun and absorb heat when their body temperature drops below the comfort zone, but move into shade when the ambient temperature starts increasing. Some species are capable of burrowing into the soil to hide and escape from the above-ground heat.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: In which of the following interaction both partners are adversely affected?
questions.solution:
Both the species benefit in mutualism and both lose in competition in their interactions with each other. In both parasitism and predation, only one species benefits (parasite and predator, respectively) and the interaction is detrimental to the other species (host and prey, respectively). The interaction where one species is benefitted and the other is neither benefitted nor harmed is called commensalism. In amensalism, one species is harmed whereas the other is
unaffected.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: In commensalism,
options: weaker is benefitted while stronger is unharmed
weaker is harmed while stronger is benefitted
questions.solution:
The relationship where one organism benefits without harming the other is called commensalism. In it, one of the two species obtain food or benefits from other without benefitting or harming the other species.

Classic example is between cattle and egret.

In commensalism, one organism benefits from the other without affecting it. Commensalism is a relation between individuals of two species in which one species obtains food or other benefits from the other without either harming or benefiting the latter.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Exponential growth occurs when there is
questions.solution: Exponential growth in a population occurs when the resources are abundant in the environment and organism is not faced by any resistance from the environment like calamities.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: In a particular geographical area, if leopards and lions feed on similar prey, they may show __________.
questions.solution: When organisms of different species compete for same resources, such struggle is called interspecific struggle. Leopard and lions show interspecific struggle as they have similar prey. The species with a lower growth rate and reproducing ability will not survive.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: What dictates the type of animals that can be supported in any area?
options: Topography, soil composition and grain size
questions.solution: On different places of Earth, nature and properties of soil are also different. These properties depend on climate, weathering process etc. Different characteristics of soil like soil composition, grain size and aggregation determine the percolation and water holding capacity of soils. These characteristics along with parameters such as pH, mineral composition and topography determine to a large extent the vegetation in any area and this vegetation dictates the type of animals that can be supported in a particular area.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: The process in which the fitness of one species (measured in terms of 'r') is significantly lower in the presence of another species, is called
questions.solution: Competition is an interaction in which the ﬁtness of one species is signiﬁcantly lowers in the presence of another species. Competition is best deﬁned as a process in which the ﬁtness of one species (measured in term of its 'r' the intrinsic rate of increase) is signiﬁcantly lower in the presence of another species. In Predation One organism feed on any other organism. In Parasitism one organism depend on other organism for food and shelter. In Commensalism one member is benefitted while other member is neither benefitted nor in loss.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which one of the following statements is incorrect?
options: In amensalism one species is harmed and other is benefited.
Commensalism is the interaction in which one species benefits and the other is neither harmed  nor benefited.
The association of cattle egret and grazing cattle is a classic example of commensalism.
Competition occurs when closely related species complete for the same resources.
questions.solution:
Amensalism is a type of biological association between two organisms where one of the two remains unaffected while the other is adversely affected by the relationship.

Classic example amensalism is displayed between fungus Penicillium and bacteria where Penicillium secretes antibiotic that inhibits the growth of bacteria (adversely affected) and Penicillium remains unaffected.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: The number of individuals of the population who left the habitat and gone elsewhere during the time period is called:
questions.solution:
Mortality is the measure of death rate in a population whereas natality is the measure of birth rate for a given population.

The number of individual people who have entered a new population group from outside for a particular period of time is called immigration.

The number of individuals of the population who left the habitat and gone elsewhere during the time period is called emigration.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Vertical distribution of different species occupying different levels is called
questions.solution: Stratification is the structure or recognizable pattern in the spatial arrangement of the members of the communities. More specifically stratification represents vertical zonation in the community. The vertical distribution of different species occupying different levels is called stratification.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Select the incorrect statement.
options: Mammals from colder climates generally have shorter ears and limbs to minimise heat loss.
Many desert plants have a thick cuticle on their leaf surfaces and have their stomata arranged in deep pits (sunken) to minimise water loss through transpiration.
During altitude sickness, the body compensates low oxygen availability by increasing red blood cell production, increasing the binding affinity of haemoglobin and by increasing breathing rate.
Desert lizards manage to keep their body temperature fairly constant by behavioural means.
questions.solution: During altitude sickness, the body compensates low oxygen availability by increasing red blood cell production, decreasing the binding affinity of haemoglobin and by increasing breathing rate.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Find the odd one out with respect to ecto- or endo-parasitism.
questions.solution: Plasmodium is an endoparasite which lives within the red blood corpuscles of man to whom it is transmitted by the bite of an infected female mosquito. Thus the parasite has two hosts-man and Anopheles-and there is an alternation of the hosts in its life-cycle.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: A population has more young individuals compared to the older individuals. What would be the status of the population after some years?
options: It will first decline and then stabilise
questions.solution: A population with more members have more chances of making more progenies. This is due to the young individuals of the populations are in the reproductive age group. Thus, more young individuals in a group will lead to a greater number of births and increase the natality over mortality. Such population is considered to be expanding population and its population after some years will increase.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: What type of human population is represented by the following age pyramid?
questions.solution: This age pyramid represents the declining population of any organism. Population decline is the reduction over time in region's census. It can be caused for several reasons that includes heavy immigration disease, famine or sub-replacement fertility.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Select the correct statement regarding population interaction.
options: Commensalism when none of the interacting populations affect each other.
Symbiosis when the interaction is useful to both the populations.
Protocooperation when one population harm other population.
Amensalism when the interaction is useful to both the populations.
questions.solution: Mutualism or symbiosis: Here both the organisms in the association are mutually benefitted and further this association is obligatory, i.e., necessary for the existence of both organisms.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: A population growing in a habitat with limited resources shows four phases of growth in the following sequence-
questions.solution: A population growing in a habitat with limited resources shows initially a lag phase, followed by phases of acceleration and deceleration and finally an asymptote when the population density reaches carrying capacity.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Which of the following graph corresponds to a population of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2000</mn></math> individuals, with <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>800</mn></math> births and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1200</mn></math> deaths over a given period of time?
questions.solution: Here, the number of deaths are more than the number of births i.e. mortality rate is greater than the natality rate. Hence the population is a declining population.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: (+,-) type of population interaction is represented by:
questions.solution: The (+,-) symbols can be applicable for both predation and parasitism. But according to the question, it is denoting parasitism. Parasites that feed on the external surface of the host organism are called ectoparasites. The most familiar examples of this group are lice on humans and ticks on dogs. Many marine fishes are infested with ectoparasitic copepods. Cuscuta, a parasitic plant that is commonly found growing on hedge plants, has lost its chlorophyll and leaves in the course of evolution. It derives its nutrition from the host plant which it parasitises.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: When resources are limited, populations exhibit logistic growth. In logistic growth, population expansion decreases as resources become scarce, levelling off when the carrying capacity of the environment is reached, resulting in a __________ curve.
questions.solution: Logistic growth: No population of any species in nature has at its disposal unlimited resources to permit exponential growth. This leads to competition between individuals for limited resources. Eventually, the ‘fittest’ individual will survive and reproduce. In nature, a given habitat has enough resources to support a maximum possible number, beyond which no further growth is possible. This limit of nature is called carrying capacity (K) for that species in that habitat. A population growing in a habitat with limited resources show initially a lag phase, followed by phases of acceleration and deceleration and finally an asymptote when the population density reaches the carrying capacity. A plot of N in relation to time (t) results in a sigmoid curve.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: About _____ of all insects are known to feed on green plants.
questions.solution: Phytophagous (herbivore predator) are those insects which fees on trees. These group comprise nearly 25% of the total insect population. They consume the plant sap. Plants have developed various ways to overcome the predation of phytophagus as plants cannot run away. Thorns, chemicals are ways to keep insect attack at bay.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: A population has a stable growth. The shape of the pyramid will be?
questions.solution:
There are three types of age pyramids.

(a) TRIANGULAR: It is a graphic representation of a young or growing population which appears like a triangle. The population has a very high proportion of pre-reproductive individuals, proportionate numbers of reproductive individuals are moderate and post-reproductive individuals are proportionately fewer. Because of the very large number of pre-reproductive individuals, more and more of them enter the reproductive phase and rapidly increases the size of the population.
(b) BELL-SHAPED:  The pyramid is bell-like with pre-reproductive individuals being only marginally more than the reproductive individuals. The population is said to be mature or stable as there is no increase or decrease in its size due to growth rate being almost zero.
(c) URN-SHAPED: It has a small number of pre-reproductive individuals followed by a large number of reproductive individuals. As there are fewer individuals in the pre-reproductive group, the population size will decline with time. Such a population shows a declined growth (negative growth).

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Biomass available for consumers and the rate of formation of new organic matter by consumers are respectively:
options: Gross primary productivity and net primary productivity
Net primary productivity and gross primary productivity
Gross primary productivity and secondary productivity
Net primary productivity and secondary productivity
questions.solution: Total biomass produced by producers is called gross primary productivity (GPP). In producers, some energy or biomass is utilized in respiration and other metabolic processes, so available biomass to next trophic level i.e. primary consumers are called net primary productivity (NPP). In these consumers, some amount of biomass is utilized in respiration and other metabolic processes and the remaining amount is assimilated in tissues, which is called as secondary productivity.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Read the following statements and choose the incorrect statement.
options: Mango tree do not and cannot grow in tropical countries like Canada and Germany
Snow leopards are not found in Kerala forests
Tuna fish are rarely caught beyond tropical latitudes in the ocean.

Both  <math><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></mrow></mfenced><mo> </mo><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">a</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">n</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">d</mi><mo> </mo><mo> </mo><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></mrow></mfenced></math>  are correct
questions.solution: Every organisms have ability to adapt with organisms and every organisms can grow optimally in suitable environment or habitat. Like for growth of mango trees comparatively high temperature is required which can be available in tropical regions. Canada and Germany are included in a temperate region where higher temperature can not be obtained.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Resource partitioning is a mechanism which has been used to promote co-existence among closely related species rather than exclusion. In MacArthur's studies, he showed that species of warblers living on the same tree avoided competition due to
options: timing differences in their feeding patterns.
both behavourial and timing differences in foraging and feeding patterns, respectively.
certain differences in behaviour which had nothing to do with foraging or feeding.
questions.solution: More recent studies do not support such gross generalisations about competition. While they do not rule out the occurrence of interspecific competition in nature, they point out that species facing competition might evolve mechanisms that promote co-existence rather than exclusion. One such mechanism is ‘resource partitioning’. If two species compete for the same resource, they could avoid competition by choosing, for instance, different times for feeding or different foraging patterns. MacArthur showed that five closely related species of warblers living on the same tree were able to avoid competition and co-exist due to behavioural differences in their foraging activities.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: The number of immigration is more than emigration and death are lower than natality. Growth curve of the population will show:
questions.solution: In any population, when the sum of immigration and natality is more than the sum of emigration and death rate, then the overall population or population density is increased. Human population show a sigmoid growth curve in which mainly 4 phases are there - <math><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">a</mi></mrow></mfenced></math> Lag phase - growth is comparatively slow. <math><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">b</mi></mrow></mfenced></math> Exponential phase - Growth is very high and continuously increasing. <math><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">c</mi></mrow></mfenced></math> Declining phase - growth is decreased. <math><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">d</mi></mrow></mfenced></math> Steady phase - growth is zero or stationary.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Amazon rain forests are considered as 'lungs of the planet' as they contribute _____ of the total oxygen in the Earth's atmosphere.
questions.solution:
The tropical Amazonian rain forest in South America has the greatest diversity.

Tropical habitats are relatively more constant and less seasonal. Such environments tend to promote niche specialization that gives more diversity. Also, such environments remain undisturbed for millions of years leading to evolution and species diversification.

Amazon rain forests are considered as 'lungs of the planet' as they contribute 20% of the total oxygen in the Earth's atmosphere.
